podcast.title: Flair Records Subsidiary
podcast.body: Flair Records, the label to which The Flares signed, was a subsidiary of Modern Records. "They decided to go with modern records, and ended up signing to Flair Records, one of modern subsidiaries."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Home for The Cliques and Solo Jesse Belvin
podcast.body: Modern Records was the label for The Cliques, the duo Jesse Belvin formed with Eugene Church, which released the commercially successful "The Girl in My Dreams." Belvin later signed with Modern Records as a solo artist, recording new material before eventually moving to RCA. "He signed to modern records as a solo artist and went into the studio to record a new song."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Marvin Phillips' New Home for Marvin and Johnny
podcast.body: After Jesse Belvin was drafted, Marvin Phillips continued their duo as Marvin and Johnny and subsequently moved over to Modern Records. The label became the home for their hits, including "Cherry Pie," and also for Jesse Belvin's later solo work and his duo The Cliques. "Marvin decided to continue the duo without Jesse, renaming it Marvin and Johnny and moved over to modern records."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Owned by Beharry Brothers
podcast.body: Modern Records was owned by the Beharry Brothers, who also employed Ike Turner as a producer for bands like The Flares. "now working for the Beharry Brothers, who owned modern records."

podcast.title: Sam Phillips' Studio as Recording Hub
podcast.body: Many artists signed to Modern Records, including The Blue Flames, predominantly recorded their music at Sam Phillips's studio, highlighting the studio's importance as a recording center. "though as with many modern records acts, they were recording mostly in Sam Phillips's studio."
